statement: For n=2d, the uniform law on the radius-sqrt(n+2) Euclidean ball is isotropic log-concave. For every balanced orthogonal split X=(U,V), f=|U|^2-|V|^2 satisfies Var(f)/[E Var(f|U)+E Var(f|V)]=(n+4)/4, and its global Poincare ratio is (n+2)/(2(n+4)). Maximal block correlation is at least n/(n+4). Thus isotropic log-concavity cannot yield a uniform balanced-block conditional-variance comparison.
assumptions: uniform law on the stated full-dimensional ball
proof_or_counterexample: PEER_AUDIT.md: radial fourth moments and rotation give Var(A)=Var(B)=d and Cov(A,B)=-d^2/(d+2). Uniform conditional balls give P f+Q f=(1+d/(d+2))f. Projection orthogonality yields the exact variance ratio. Rotational invariance covers all balanced orthogonal splits.
